title: Roman numerals both ways
prompt:
Read lines from standard input and convert each one. Spaces at the start and end of a line are ignored, and a line that is then empty is skipped.

- A line made only of decimal digits is a number. If its value is between 1 and 3999 print its Roman numeral in the standard form (M, CM, D, CD, C, XC, L, XL, X, IX, V, IV, I; for example 1994 is `MCMXCIV`). Leading zeros are allowed (`007` is 7). Any other value prints `INVALID`.
- A line made only of the uppercase letters I V X L C D M is a Roman numeral. If it is written in exactly the standard form, with no other spelling of the same value (so `IIII`, `VX`, `IC` and `MMMM` are not valid), print its value as a decimal number. Otherwise print `INVALID`.
- Anything else prints `INVALID`.

Print one result per non-skipped line.
